summary: This program stores the number 42 in a variable and prints it to the console. It is the same shape as the reminder example, but the variable holds a number instead of text.

lines.text: The type comes first: `int` tells Java this variable holds a whole number, so the value 42 is stored as a number rather than as text. Try changing 42 to your own favorite number and running the program again.
There are no quotation marks around `number`, so Java prints the value stored in the variable rather than the word "number". Wrapping it in quotes is the most common beginner slip here.
